evaluation.heading: How to Evaluate a Titanium Dioxide Grade
evaluation.intro: Use the application, process classification when relevant, grade-specific technical data, destination requirements and buyer validation as separate evaluation inputs.

items.title: Define the application
items.body: Record the resin or material system, end use, processing conditions and performance targets that the grade must be evaluated against.

items.title: Confirm whether process matters
items.body: Identify whether chloride or sulfate production-process classification is a required sourcing parameter. Process classification does not determine application suitability.

items.title: Review applicable technical data
items.body: Review information issued for the grade you are evaluating. Do not infer missing values from another grade, an older source or an unrelated TDS.

items.title: Identify destination and document needs
items.body: Confirm the destination market and the technical, quality, compliance or origin documents required for the applicable request.

items.title: Validate in the buyer's system
items.body: Confirm final suitability through the buyer's own formulation, processing conditions, performance requirements and qualification process.

items.title: Review by Application
items.body: Review grades listed for each application and continue to detailed application guidance.

items.title: Identify Required Documents
items.body: Review technical, quality, compliance and origin-document pathways for the applicable request.

items.title: Review Destination Context
items.body: Review destination-market procurement context without assuming local availability, registration or regulatory acceptance.

buyerQuestions.question: How do I choose a titanium dioxide pigment grade?
buyerQuestions.answer: Start with the intended application, then use production-process classification if it is a required sourcing parameter. Review the relevant grade page and confirm the available product information against the formulation, processing conditions, destination and documentation requirements. A listed result is a starting point for evaluation, not a suitability guarantee.

buyerQuestions.question: Which grades are listed in this product center?
What is the difference between application and process selection?
buyerQuestions.answer: Application selection groups grades by listed use-case relationships, while process selection groups grades by their production-process classification. A process classification does not determine application suitability on its own.

buyerQuestions.question: What if no grade is shown for my application?
buyerQuestions.answer: A missing result means that the selector has no listed grade for that application. It should not automatically be interpreted as a technical rejection of every grade. Buyers can contact the team when a requirement is not represented in the selector.

buyerQuestions.question: Does a listed grade guarantee suitability?
buyerQuestions.answer: No. A listed grade is a starting point for technical evaluation. Final suitability should be confirmed against the buyer's formulation, processing conditions, performance requirements, destination requirements and applicable documentation.
